newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil sees profit challenges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil sees profit challenges.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd managing director and chief executive officer Norb Cole said on Tuesday that there are still challenges on revenue and profits but that he was confident that this could be overcome in future years.
Cole told a luncheon at the Australia-Isreal Chamber of Commerce that sales volumes in Australia were expected to rise between six and seven percent in 1996.

"There have been, and still are, some challenges on the revenue and profit line, but given the strengthening of our competitive position, our significant increase in people numbers ... and the strategic expenditure of capital during the year, I am confident that these problems can be overcome in future years," he said.
Cole said Australia, which is the company's largest single operation is recording an increase in sales volume of six to seven percent, as the calendar year drew to a close.

"Australia is still CCA's largest single operation and we are very pleased to report that this key market, which some have mistakenly termed 'mature', is recording an increase in sales volume of 6-7 percent as we close out the year," Cole said.

C-C Amatil's share price has been sharply sold off in the past two trading sessions after the company said late on Friday it expected a flat result in calendar 1996. In August, it had said it expected profits to rise by 10 percent in 1996.
Cole said today the profit warning reflected the current retail environment in Australia as well as the 16 other countries in which it operates.

"Notwithstanding last Friday's announcement, the fundamentals of CCA's global business are as robust as ever and in fact, 1996 will be another record breaking year in terms of our sales volume, growth and market share gains, particularly in Europe," Cole said.
He said despite certain fluctations in year-on-year profit growth, C-C Amatil's basic growth strategies were on track and on target to deliver "solid value increases over time".
Cole siad C-C Amatil is expected to sell about 800 million unit cases of soft drink in 1996, up from 587 million in 1995 and compared with 240 million in 1990.
Shares in C-C Amatil, is about 36 percent owned by The Coca-Cola Company, were 52 cents lower at A$14.98 at 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) on Tuesday, after having closed at A$17.54 on Friday.
